mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced cost of capital for corporate investment.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods of declining FEDFUNDS are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 7.5% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 7.5% (i.e., the negative return prediction fails).

mechanism_narrative: Jointly rising housing starts (HOUST) and GDP growth (GDPC1) over the prior 3 months signal robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days via increased corporate investment and consumption expenditure.
failure_condition: The interaction term (HOUST growth * GDPC1 growth) fails to produce positive returns in more than 40% of instances where both series rise (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% YoY), a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary tightening that reduces risk appetite and increases discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The signal fails when 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rises (i.e., negative return prediction incorrect).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production (INDPRO) decline exceeding 0.5% from the prior month indicates weakening manufacturing output, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate production and earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 100,000 jobs signals strong labor market conditions, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through elevated consumer confidence and immediate spending growth.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods of PAYEMS growth > 100k.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market expansion (HOUST growth > 0.5% monthly) combined with GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.0% annualized signals sustained economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through prolonged corporate investment cycles and earnings momentum.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where both HOUST growth > 0.5% and GDPC1 growth > 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% YoY signals easing inflation, which compresses discount rates and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through reduced real interest rate pressure on equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods of CPIAUCSL decline below 2.0%.
